facts.label: Identity and perimeter
facts.text: - The registrant is the same in every filing. The Q3 10-Q cover reads "Encompass Health Corporation (Exact name of Registrant as specified in its Charter)" (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:1), with Commission File Number 001-10315. The 10-K carries the same file number and registrant name (10-K_2025-12-31, page:1). - Perimeter: the statements are consolidated and include noncontrolling interests. The Q3 10-Q states "We are the sole owner of 110 of these hospitals. We retain 50.0% to 97.5% ownership in the remaining 67 jointly owned hospitals." (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:12). Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests is shown separately as "Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests (53.7) (48.1) (160.9) (135.9)" (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:7), so leverage and coverage metrics on the consolidated perimeter include debt and earnings of partly owned hospitals. - Borrower, guarantor and issuer roles: the Q3 10-Q says the credit agreement and the senior notes "are guaranteed by certain consolidated subsidiaries" and that the guarantees "are full and unconditional and joint and several" (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:44). Summarized financial information for the parent and subsidiary guarantors on a combined basis is given for nine months 2026 and at 2026-09-30 and 2025-12-31 (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:45). The list of guarantor subsidiaries (Exhibit 22) is listed in the exhibit index (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:51) but the exhibit text is not in the pack. Which subsidiaries guarantee remains unresolved, and it is a gap, not a blocker, because the consolidated issuer is clear. - Restricted and unrestricted entities: no source defines unrestricted subsidiaries. Variable interest entities are disclosed: "total assets of variable interest entities of $213.6 million" and "total liabilities of the variable interest entities of $51.2 million" at 2026-09-30 (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:8). - The company reports one segment: "We manage our operations using one operating segment which is also our reportable segment: inpatient rehabilitation." (10-K_2025-12-31, page:216).

facts.label: Source-by-source assessment
facts.text: - Annual report (10-K, FY2025, 217 pages). Audited, original authority for FY2025 and prior-year comparatives. Contains the debt note (page:198, page:199), segment note with Adjusted EBITDA (page:216, page:217), the MD&A liquidity and contractual obligations discussion (page:133 to page:135) and the exhibit list (page:152 to page:156). The debt note shows year-end 2025 borrowings: "Advances under revolving credit facility $ 130.0 $ 20.0" and the covenant statement "The maximum leverage ratio in the financial covenants is 4.50x as of December 31, 2025." (10-K_2025-12-31, page:198 and page:199). The 10-K describes a credit agreement whose revolver matures in October 2027; the Q3 10-Q says a replacement agreement was entered into, so the 10-K debt terms are superseded in part (see the conflict register below). - Q1 2026 10-Q (49 pages). Unaudited. Shows revolver availability of "approximately $726 million available to us under our revolving credit facility" at 2026-03-31 (10-Q_2026-03-31, page:37). Retained as a separate source and not collapsed into the later reports. - Q2 2026 10-Q (52 pages). Unaudited. Shows "approximately $746 million available to us under our revolving credit facility" at 2026-06-30 (10-Q_2026-06-30, page:40). Retained separately. - Q3 2026 10-Q (51 pages). Unaudited and the most recent filing before the cutoff. It is the controlling source for the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, debt note, liquidity text and covenant levels. Key located content: balance sheet "Cash and cash equivalents $ 76.2 $ 72.2" and "Total assets(1) $ 7,566.5 $ 7,089.7" (page:8); debt table "Advances under revolving credit facility $ 75.0 $ 130.0", "5.875% Senior Notes due 2034 588.2 —", "Finance lease obligations 274.9 294.6" and "Total $ 2,630.0 $ 2,599.1" (page:17); "we had approximately $871 million available to us under our revolving credit facility" (page:40); and covenant text "the maximum leverage ratio requirement per our credit agreement was 4.50x and the minimum interest coverage ratio requirement was 3.0x, and we were in compliance with these covenants" (page:40). It also has the nine-month cash flow summary (page:41), contractual obligations (page:41 and page:42), and an Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation "Adjusted EBITDA $ 346.6 $ 300.1 $ 1,043.4 $ 932.3" (page:25). - Q1, Q2 and Q3 earnings slides (EX-99.2, 17, 19 and 20 pages). Management presentations: attributed supporting claims only. The Q3 deck gives a debt schedule with "Debt to Adjusted EBITDA 1.9x 2.0x" and "Leverage net of cash and cash equivalents 1.8x 1.9x" (EX-99.2_2026-10-28, page:11), revolver position "$871 Available $75 Drawn + $54 reserved for LCs" (same page), updated 2026 guidance "Adjusted EBITDA(3) $1,365 to $1,395 $1,395 to $1,415" (EX-99.2_2026-10-28, page:7), and a reconciliation of net income to Adjusted EBITDA (EX-99.2_2026-10-28, page:13). The Q1 deck guidance table is on its page:7 and its debt schedule on its page:10; the Q2 deck debt schedule is on its page:11.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is adequate for a consolidated credit snapshot. Reported figures reconcile: operating expense lines sum to the printed totals, the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation returns to pre-tax income, and the debt table ties to the balance sheet and to the maturity table. Encompass Health is a low-leverage, cash-generative issuer on the evidence supplied: total debt to trailing four quarter Adjusted EBITDA is 1.88x at Q3 2026, net debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 1.83x, EBITDA to interest excluding amortization is 11.7x, and revolver availability is about $871m. The 2026 refinancing moved the revolver maturity from October 2027 to March 2031 and replaced $400m of the 2028 notes with 2034 notes, so no bond matures before the remaining $400m of 2028 notes. Three points temper the view. First, the company deducts net income attributable to noncontrolling interests inside Adjusted EBITDA while reporting debt on a fully consolidated basis, and only part of the group guarantees the notes. Second, free cash flow after capex, noncontrolling distributions, dividends and buybacks was negative for nine months 2026, so debt rose while revenue and EBITDA grew. Third, the covenants are stated as compliance only, and the agreements that define them are not in the pack. The leverage and coverage figures below are therefore analyst calculations on carrying values and reported Adjusted EBITDA, and are not the covenant ratios.

facts.label: Liquidity
facts.text: Liquidity at 30 September 2026 is cash and cash equivalents of $76.2 million plus about $871 million available under the $1 billion revolver, "approximately $871 million available to us under our revolving credit facility" (10-Q Q3 page:40). The availability reconciles to the commitment: 1,000 less 75.0 drawn less 53.6 letters of credit (10-Q Q3 page:20) equals 871.4. The deck shows the same split, "$871 Available $75 Drawn + $54 reserved for LCs" (deck Q3 page:11). Restricted cash of 24.0 and restricted marketable securities of 158.5 are excluded (10-Q Q3 page:40). Total liquidity on this basis is 947.2. The revolver matures 9 March 2031 (10-Q Q3 page:18), so no facility expires within twelve months of the cutoff. The only maturities within twelve months are scheduled amortization of 9.2 in the remainder of 2026 and 47.0 in 2027 on the face basis (10-Q Q3 page:17); the 12 months from 30 September 2026 therefore include 9.2 plus part of the 47.0.

facts.label: Cash flow quality
facts.text: Cash interest has two definitions in the sources. The 10-K reports cash paid for interest of 133.1 in FY2025 (10-K page:166) while management's "cash interest payments (net of amortization of debt discounts and fees)" are 113.6 for 2025 and 90.2 for nine months 2026 (deck Q3 page:8). The 113.6 equals the 123.2 interest expense less 9.6 of amortization (10-K page:165), so the deck measure is an accrual-based figure rather than cash paid. Interest capitalized was 17.6 in FY2025 (10-K page:196), which explains part of the gap between cash paid and expense. The Q3 10-Q omits cash paid for interest from its supplemental cash flow disclosure (10-Q Q3 page:11), so a cash-paid basis cannot be extended to Q3 2026.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Encompass Health is the largest owner and operator of inpatient rehabilitation hospitals on its own description, with 177 hospitals in 39 states and Puerto Rico at 30 September 2026, 67 of them joint ventures. There is no leveraged buyout, sponsor, acquisition or restructuring in the pack: the transactions in the period are financings, a small equity-method disposal, a litigation recovery and shareholder distributions. The business is a single segment whose revenue is set largely by government reimbursement, so the creditor risk mechanics run through Medicare rate updates, claim review and denial rules, labor cost inflation and the pace of capacity additions, rather than through sponsor behaviour. The sources show a company that has funded growth with operating cash flow and the revolver while raising dividends and buybacks, and that refinanced half of its 2028 notes into 2034 notes at a higher coupon. Credit-relevant strengths are the nondiscretionary patient base, referral dependence on acute-care hospitals that is also a joint-venture channel, and long-dated fixed-rate debt. Credit-relevant weaknesses are payor concentration, regulatory review expansion from 2027, a billing disruption that lifted bad debt reserves in Q3 2026, geographic concentration in Florida and Texas and a growth plan that consumes more cash than operations generate after distributions. Ownership, control rights and sponsor alignment cannot be assessed beyond the public-company facts, because the proxy statement is not in the pack.

There is no leveraged buyout, sponsor, acquisition or restructuring in the pack: the transactions in the period are financings, a small equity-method disposal, a litigation recovery and shareholder distributions. The business is a single segment whose revenue is set largely by government reimbursement, so the creditor risk mechanics run through Medicare rate updates, claim review and denial rules, labor cost inflation and the pace of capacity additions, rather than through sponsor behaviour. The sources show a company that has funded growth with operating cash flow and the revolver while raising dividends and buybacks, and that refinanced half of its 2028 notes into 2034 notes at a higher coupon. Credit-relevant strengths are the nondiscretionary patient base, referral dependence on acute-care hospitals that is also a joint-venture channel, and long-dated fixed-rate debt. Credit-relevant weaknesses are payor concentration, regulatory review expansion from 2027, a billing disruption that lifted bad debt reserves in Q3 2026, geographic concentration in Florida and Texas and a growth plan that consumes more cash than operations generate after distributions. Ownership, control rights and sponsor alignment cannot be assessed beyond the public-company facts, because the proxy statement is not in the pack.

facts.text: There is no sponsor transaction, acquisition or restructuring in the sources, so the transaction fact pack is a record of 2026 financing and capital events, all executed and all disclosed in the Q3 10-Q (Documentary Fact). On 9 March 2026 the company signed the 2026 Credit Agreement with Truist Bank as administrative and collateral agent, replacing the 2022 agreement that had Barclays as agent. Terms are described as substantially the same except a maturity of 9 March 2031, an undrawn fee lowered by five basis points, relaxed limits on investments, debt, liens and restricted payments, removal of a 0.10% adjustment on Term SOFR borrowings and a swingline sublimit raised from $25 million to $40 million; a $250.0 million revolver draw repaid the 2022 agreement in full (10-Q Q3 page:18). The agreement is secured by personal property of the company and its subsidiary guarantors. The agreement itself is not in the pack, so the relaxation of restricted payment and debt limits cannot be sized.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: In May 2026 the company issued $500 million of 5.875% Senior Notes due 2034 at par for about $491 million of net proceeds, redeemed $400 million of the $800 million 4.50% Senior Notes due 2028 at par and repaid $100 million of revolver borrowings, recording a $3.2 million loss on early extinguishment in Q2 2026. In August 2026 it issued a further $100 million of the 2034 notes at 98.75% for about $97 million of net proceeds, used with cash to repay revolver borrowings (10-Q Q3 page:19). The liquidity effect is that revolver drawings fell to 75.0 at 30 September 2026 and availability rose to about $871 million, while total debt at carrying value rose by 108.3 over nine months 2026 (CP-1 reference; deck Q3 page:8). The coupon effect is that the weighted coupon on senior notes rises to 4.99% from 4.63% (Analyst Interpretation, see Calculations): the remaining 2028 notes at $400 million face are callable at par, and the 2034 notes are callable beginning June 2029 per the deck chart (deck Q3 page:11). The use of proceeds to retire lower-coupon debt rather than to fund distributions shows a refinancing motive, though total debt rose in the same period that dividends and buybacks rose.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: Medicare 66.3% and Medicare Advantage 15.7% of Q3 2026 revenue and 92% of patients admitted from acute-care hospitals (10-Q Q3 page:33; 10-K page:9). Mechanic: nondiscretionary demand supports volume, but nearly all price-setting is administrative, so a rule change reprices most revenue at once and referral channels depend on acute-care partners. Implication: revenue visibility is high on volume and low on rate; debt service capacity depends on regulatory outcomes more than on competition. Counter-evidence: the pack contains no logged conflict against this. 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Medicare rate update of about 2.3% against assumed labor cost growth per FTE of 3.5% to 4.0% (10-Q Q3 page:31; deck Q3 page:7); bad debt reserves up to 2.7% of revenue from 1.9% (deck Q3 page:5); review expansion to 108 hospitals from 1 Jan 2027 (10-Q Q3 page:31). Mechanic: a price-cost gap and slower collections reduce EBITDA and cash conversion together. Implication: leverage of 1.88x leaves cushion, but a combined margin and collection shock would reduce the cash available for growth capex and distributions first. The conflicting account-receivable figures logged below limit how precisely cash conversion can be traced. 3. Concentration risk. Evidence: Florida and Texas beds of 3,710 out of 11,465 and a single segment (10-K page:110, page:216). Mechanic: state-level events hit a third of capacity. Implication: modest diversification within a single reimbursement system. 4. Sponsor alignment. Not applicable as a sponsor concept: the company is listed with no named sponsor. Alignment is with public shareholders through dividends and buybacks, which were partly debt-funded in nine months 2026. Implication: monitor distribution pace against free cash flow after growth capex. 5. Key uncertainties. Control and ownership detail, covenant definitions, guarantor list and the duration of the billing disruption are not evidenced.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: - Weighted coupon on senior notes before the 2026 issues: (800 x 4.50% + 800 x 4.75% + 400 x 4.625%) = 36.00 + 38.00 + 18.50 = 92.50 on 2,000 = 4.625%, shown as 4.63%. Face amounts as in the financial base: 4.50% notes 800 before the May 2026 redemption, 4.75% notes 800, 4.625% notes 400. - After: (400 x 4.50% + 800 x 4.75% + 400 x 4.625% + 600 x 5.875%) = 18.00 + 38.00 + 18.50 + 35.25 = 109.75 on 2,200 = 4.989%, shown as 4.99%. The revolver is excluded. - Gross annual coupon on the new 2034 notes less the retired 2028 notes: 600 x 5.875% = 35.25 less 400 x 4.50% = 18.00 gives 17.25 per year, before interest saved on the revolver. - Florida and Texas beds: 1,718 + 1,992 = 3,710; 3,710 / 11,465 = 32.4% of licensed beds at 31 Dec 2025. Hospitals: 25 + 29 = 54 of 173 = 31.2%. - Medicare and Medicare Advantage share, Q3 2026: 66.3% + 15.7% = 82.0%; nine months 2026: 65.7% + 16.1% = 81.8%. The 10-K reports approximately 82% for FY2025 (10-K page:23). - Hospitals: 110 wholly owned + 67 joint ventures = 177 (10-Q Q3 page:12). - Distributions against cash flow, nine months 2026, using the financial base: dividends 57.9 + buybacks 203.7 = 261.6; operating cash flow 957.7 less capex 617.2 less noncontrolling distributions 141.8 = 198.7; 198.7 - 261.6 = -62.9. - Accounts receivable change: 712.0 - 619.2 = 92.8 between 31 Dec 2025 and 30 Sep 2026, against revenue growth shown in the financial base. No days-sales ratio is calculated, because period-matched revenue and a consistent receivable definition are not both supplied (see the receivable conflict). - Q3 2026 buyback: 57.9 from the deck, not derived.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Encompass Health Corp is a moderately leveraged, cash-generative inpatient rehabilitation operator whose credit is sound but exposed to government reimbursement. Its strongest support is financial: total debt was 1.88x trailing Adjusted EBITDA at Q3 2026, liquidity was USD 947.2 million, and the first bond maturity is USD 400 million face of 2028 notes. Its weakest point is that Medicare and Medicare Advantage supplied 82.0% of Q3 2026 revenue, so price updates and claim-review rules can move earnings quickly, while cash flow after capex, partner distributions, dividends and buybacks was negative USD 62.9 million in nine months 2026. The outcome depends on whether review expansion from 1 January 2027 and the billing disruption erode cash conversion before the issuer slows growth capex or shareholder returns.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Interest cover is high: Adjusted EBITDA covered interest excluding amortization 11.7x on a trailing basis at Q3 2026 against a 3.0x covenant minimum [CP-1 Chart data: interest cover] (Analyst Interpretation); cash paid for interest in FY2025 gave 9.5x on the annual report figure, so the basis matters.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. The issuer has modest leverage, with total debt at 1.88x trailing Adjusted EBITDA at Q3 2026, and wide room under the 4.50x covenant maximum (Analyst Interpretation, CP-1 Chart data: leverage). It has ample liquidity of USD 947.2 million and no revolver expiry until March 2031 (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Liquidity). Its notes carry fixed coupons, with the first bond maturity in 2028 (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Debt by instrument). Demand is nondiscretionary, with 92% of patients admitted from acute-care hospitals, and 67 of 177 hospitals are joint ventures that tie the issuer to referring systems (Documentary Fact, CP-1A Company and operating model). Growth capex is largely discretionary, since only about USD 225 million to USD 240 million of 2026 capex is nondiscretionary against a total of about USD 920 million to USD 995 million (Documentary Fact, CP-1A Company and operating model), which gives the issuer a lever to protect cash in a downturn. Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 346.6 million in Q3 2026 against USD 300.1 million (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Financials and credit metrics).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. The issuer depends on one payor class for most revenue, with Medicare and Medicare Advantage at 82.0% of Q3 2026 revenue, so a single rule change reprices most of the book (Documentary Fact, CP-1A Company and operating model). Review Choice Demonstration coverage will reach 108 hospitals from 1 January 2027 and bad debt reserves are higher, which together put cash conversion at risk (Documentary Fact). Cash flow after growth capex and distributions was negative USD 62.9 million in nine months 2026, so debt rose while leverage stayed modest (Analyst Interpretation, CP-1 Cash flow quality). Adjusted EBITDA deducts net income attributable to noncontrolling interests while debt is consolidated in full, and only part of the group guarantees the notes, with the parent and guarantors producing USD 3,016.4 million of the USD 4,793.5 million nine-month 2026 revenue (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Perimeter and Findings). Florida and Texas hold 32.4% of licensed beds at 31 December 2025 (Analyst Interpretation, CP-1A Calculations). Ownership, control rights, covenant ratios, guarantor list and ratings are not evidenced (Insufficient Information, CP-0 Gaps), and missing evidence is not read as an adverse conclusion.

facts.label: Gaps propagated
facts.text: Each limitation is stated once where it changes a conclusion. Upstream signals carried: the source pack lacks the credit agreement, indentures, guarantor list, ratings and covenant values, so the leverage and cover figures cannot be called covenant headroom and structural ranking is unconfirmed; ownership and control are Insufficient Information because the proxy statement is absent; and the business pack records no explicit readiness label for this synthesis, which keeps confidence at Medium. Four conflicts logged in the business pack stay unreconciled: the remaining buyback authorization, the accounts receivable balances in the annual report, the two cash interest definitions and the segment note against the income statement.

facts.label: Evidence trace view
facts.text: The evaluated set is traceable. I re-opened the cited pages of the pinned filings and decks for every quoted passage in the financial base and the business pack and for the numbers placed next to each locator; the quotes matched their pages and the only numbers not found on a cited page were the module's own calculations, which I recomputed. The synthesis introduces no figure that is absent from the two modules it builds on. Verdicts on the material claims are supported, with five partly supported claims whose qualifications are stated in the support review, and no claim is unsupported. I found no pair of claims from different modules that cannot both hold. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filings and slide decks identify the issuer and cover FY2025 through Q3 2026 with debt, liquidity and covenant text, so the minimum credit work can proceed with stated limitations. | Medium | No credit agreement, indentures, ratings, market prices or press releases are supplied, so covenant definitions and tranche terms rest on summaries. |

### Readiness view

The effective source set is sufficient for a limited-scope credit snapshot of Encompass Health Corporation on a consolidated basis. The filed statements and notes in the audited annual report and the three quarterly reports control the financial and debt facts. The slide decks add attributed management claims such as guidance, a debt schedule and an Adjusted EBITDA bridge, and none of them overrides a filing. The view for each requested consumer is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, because the owner can perform its method with bounded gaps. No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. No identity boundary is unresolved: every source is the consolidated filing of one registrant. The assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. This module does not assert normalized quarters, reconciliation or downstream input acceptance.
### Identity and perimeter

- The registrant is the same in every filing. The Q3 10-Q cover reads "Encompass Health Corporation (Exact name of Registrant as specified in its Charter)" (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:1), with Commission File Number 001-10315. The 10-K carries the same file number and registrant name (10-K_2025-12-31, page:1).

- Perimeter: the statements are consolidated and include noncontrolling interests. The Q3 10-Q states "We are the sole owner of 110 of these hospitals. We retain 50.0% to 97.5% ownership in the remaining 67 jointly owned hospitals." (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:12). Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests is shown separately as "Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests (53.7) (48.1) (160.9) (135.9)" (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:7), so leverage and coverage metrics on the consolidated perimeter include debt and earnings of partly owned hospitals.

- Borrower, guarantor and issuer roles: the Q3 10-Q says the credit agreement and the senior notes "are guaranteed by certain consolidated subsidiaries" and that the guarantees "are full and unconditional and joint and several" (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:44). Summarized financial information for the parent and subsidiary guarantors on a combined basis is given for nine months 2026 and at 2026-09-30 and 2025-12-31 (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:45). The list of guarantor subsidiaries (Exhibit 22) is listed in the exhibit index (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:51) but the exhibit text is not in the pack. Which subsidiaries guarantee remains unresolved, and it is a gap, not a blocker, because the consolidated issuer is clear.

- Restricted and unrestricted entities: no source defines unrestricted subsidiaries. Variable interest entities are disclosed: "total assets of variable interest entities of $213.6 million" and "total liabilities of the variable interest entities of $51.2 million" at 2026-09-30 (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:8).
- The company reports one segment: "We manage our operations using one operating segment which is also our reportable segment: inpatient rehabilitation." (10-K_2025-12-31, page:216).
### Source-by-source assessment

- Annual report (10-K, FY2025, 217 pages). Audited, original authority for FY2025 and prior-year comparatives. Contains the debt note (page:198, page:199), segment note with Adjusted EBITDA (page:216, page:217), the MD&A liquidity and contractual obligations discussion (page:133 to page:135) and the exhibit list (page:152 to page:156). The debt note shows year-end 2025 borrowings: "Advances under revolving credit facility $ 130.0 $ 20.0" and the covenant statement "The maximum leverage ratio in the financial covenants is 4.50x as of December 31, 2025." (10-K_2025-12-31, page:198 and page:199). The 10-K describes a credit agreement whose revolver matures in October 2027; the Q3 10-Q says a replacement agreement was entered into, so the 10-K debt terms are superseded in part (see the conflict register below).

- Q1 2026 10-Q (49 pages). Unaudited. Shows revolver availability of "approximately $726 million available to us under our revolving credit facility" at 2026-03-31 (10-Q_2026-03-31, page:37). Retained as a separate source and not collapsed into the later reports.
- Q2 2026 10-Q (52 pages). Unaudited. Shows "approximately $746 million available to us under our revolving credit facility" at 2026-06-30 (10-Q_2026-06-30, page:40). Retained separately.

- Q3 2026 10-Q (51 pages). Unaudited and the most recent filing before the cutoff. It is the controlling source for the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, debt note, liquidity text and covenant levels. Key located content: balance sheet "Cash and cash equivalents $ 76.2 $ 72.2" and "Total assets(1) $ 7,566.5 $ 7,089.7" (page:8); debt table "Advances under revolving credit facility $ 75.0 $ 130.0", "5.875% Senior Notes due 2034 588.2 —", "Finance lease obligations 274.9 294.6" and "Total $ 2,630.0 $ 2,599.1" (page:17); "we had approximately $871 million available to us under our revolving credit facility" (page:40); and covenant text "the maximum leverage ratio requirement per our credit agreement was 4.50x and the minimum interest coverage ratio requirement was 3.0x, and we were in compliance with these covenants" (page:40). It also has the nine-month cash flow summary (page:41), contractual obligations (page:41 and page:42), and an Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation "Adjusted EBITDA $ 346.6 $ 300.1 $ 1,043.4 $ 932.3" (page:25).

- Q1, Q2 and Q3 earnings slides (EX-99.2, 17, 19 and 20 pages). Management presentations: attributed supporting claims only. The Q3 deck gives a debt schedule with "Debt to Adjusted EBITDA 1.9x 2.0x" and "Leverage net of cash and cash equivalents 1.8x 1.9x" (EX-99.2_2026-10-28, page:11), revolver position "$871 Available $75 Drawn + $54 reserved for LCs" (same page), updated 2026 guidance "Adjusted EBITDA(3) $1,365 to $1,395 $1,395 to $1,415" (EX-99.2_2026-10-28, page:7), and a reconciliation of net income to Adjusted EBITDA (EX-99.2_2026-10-28, page:13). The Q1 deck guidance table is on its page:7 and its debt schedule on its page:10; the Q2 deck debt schedule is on its page:11.
### Period and basis labels

- Statements are Q3 2026 (three months ended 2026-09-30), nine months 2026, FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31) and balance sheets at 2026-09-30 and 2025-12-31. Deck metrics such as leverage are management-defined and labelled by quarter. Trailing four quarter statistics in the deck are labelled "Key statistics - trailing four quarters" (EX-99.2_2026-10-28, page:8).
- Currency is USD in millions except per share data: "(In Millions, Except Per Share Data)" (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:7). This matches the context reporting currency.

- Adjusted EBITDA is a company-defined measure "as defined in our credit agreement" (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:45) and reconciled to net income and operating cash flow; it is not a GAAP figure, and it is consolidated, adding back net income attributable to noncontrolling interests ("Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests 53.7 48.1 160.9 135.9", 10-Q_2026-09-30, page:25).
### Version relationships and conflicts
| Item | Earlier source | Later source | Downstream effect |

| Credit agreement | The 10-K debt note says the revolver and letter of credit subfacility, "all of which mature in October 2027" (10-K_2025-12-31, page:198) | The Q3 10-Q says "the maturity date has been changed to March 9, 2031" under the 2026 Credit Agreement (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:18) | CP-1 and CP-2 must use the 2026 terms for maturity and the 2025 filing only as year-end history. Both agreements are not in the pack, so their text is not checked. |

| Letter of credit usage | The 10-K gives "$46.3 million and $36.3 million" utilised at 2025-12-31 and 2024-12-31 (10-K_2025-12-31, page:199) | The Q3 deck shows "$54 reserved for LCs" (EX-99.2_2026-10-28, page:11) | The Q3 10-Q fair value table also shows "Letters of credit — 53.6 — 46.3" (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:20), so the deck figure is corroborated by a filing; the Q3 10-Q states availability of about $871 million directly. |

| Quarterly revolver position | Q1 10-Q, availability about $726 million | Q2 10-Q about $746 million, Q3 10-Q about $871 million | Not a conflict; these are dated observations to be kept separate by period. |

No numerical conflict between a deck and a filing was identified in the located pages for debt carrying amounts: the Q3 deck debt schedule repeats the Q3 10-Q debt table (for example "5.875% Senior Notes due 2034 588.2" in both, EX-99.2_2026-10-28 page:11 and 10-Q_2026-09-30 page:17). This is a read of the located pages, not a full line-by-line comparison.
### Coverage by profile

- Financial statements and notes: statements of operations (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:7), balance sheet (page:8), cash flows (page:10, page:11), the long-term debt note (page:17 to page:19), redeemable noncontrolling interests (page:19), fair value (page:19, page:20) and contingencies are present in the Q3 10-Q, with lease and contingency notes in the 10-K. A cash flow statement is present (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:10 and page:11).

- Debt, liquidity and covenants: present as filed text in the Q3 10-Q (page:17 to page:19, page:40 to page:45) and in the 10-K (page:198 to page:200). The revolver commitment, letter of credit subfacility, financial covenant levels and compliance statement are all located. Covenant test values reported by the issuer are not printed as a number; compliance is stated in words, which limits headroom work.

- Segment and KPI tables: one segment; service-line revenue and operating metrics are located (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:25; EX-99.2_2026-10-28, page:12). Quarter-by-quarter operating data for seven quarters appears in the Q3 deck.

- Earnings releases: the pack holds earnings slides but no earnings release 8-K text. Reconciliations of Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EPS and adjusted free cash flow are in the decks (EX-99.2_2026-10-28, pages 13 to 16) and the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation is also in the Q3 10-Q (page:24, page:25, page:47, page:48).

- Decks: text extraction only. The debt maturity chart on the Q3 deck (page:11) extracted as a run of labels and values with no axis structure, so chart reading is a parse gap. No claim is made that charts, images or speaker notes were inspected. The seven-source page counts are 217, 49, 52, 51, 17, 19 and 20, and every extracted page is retained as text.

- Legal financing sources: none supplied. The exhibit index of the 10-K lists indenture supplements and the credit agreement by reference (10-K_2025-12-31, page:152 to page:154), but their text is not in the pack.
- Workbooks and scans: none supplied.

| CP-5 | Evidence for strengths, weaknesses and risks | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Risk factors and regulatory text are in the 10-K and MD&A; no ratings, market prices or third-party research are supplied. |
### Subsequent events and cutoff

The Q3 10-Q (filed 2026-11-03, signed "Date: November 3, 2026", page:51) and the Q3 deck (October 28, 2026) fall before the cutoff 2026-11-05. No source in the pack is dated after the cutoff. Post-quarter items in the Q3 10-Q include a dividend: "On October 22, 2026, our board of directors declared a cash dividend of $0.21 per share, payable on January 15, 2027" (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:43). That is a future payment date inside a dated declaration, not a post-cutoff fact. Item 5 reports "Insider Trading Arrangements None." (10-Q_2026-09-30, page:50).

### Financial base view

The financial base is adequate for a consolidated credit snapshot. Reported figures reconcile: operating expense lines sum to the printed totals, the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation returns to pre-tax income, and the debt table ties to the balance sheet and to the maturity table. Encompass Health is a low-leverage, cash-generative issuer on the evidence supplied: total debt to trailing four quarter Adjusted EBITDA is 1.88x at Q3 2026, net debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 1.83x, EBITDA to interest excluding amortization is 11.7x, and revolver availability is about $871m. The 2026 refinancing moved the revolver maturity from October 2027 to March 2031 and replaced $400m of the 2028 notes with 2034 notes, so no bond matures before the remaining $400m of 2028 notes. Three points temper the view. First, the company deducts net income attributable to noncontrolling interests inside Adjusted EBITDA while reporting debt on a fully consolidated basis, and only part of the group guarantees the notes. Second, free cash flow after capex, noncontrolling distributions, dividends and buybacks was negative for nine months 2026, so debt rose while revenue and EBITDA grew. Third, the covenants are stated as compliance only, and the agreements that define them are not in the pack. The leverage and coverage figures below are therefore analyst calculations on carrying values and reported Adjusted EBITDA, and are not the covenant ratios.
### Perimeter, definitions and carry-forward from the readiness handoff

- Reporting entity: Encompass Health Corporation, consolidated, with 177 hospitals of which 110 are wholly owned and 67 are jointly owned at 50.0% to 97.5% (10-Q Q3 page:12). Figures below are for that consolidated perimeter, and the parent is not separately reported except in the guarantor summary (10-Q Q3 page:45).

- Adjusted EBITDA is company-defined, "Adjusted EBITDA as defined in our credit agreement" (10-Q Q3 page:45). It is reached from income before tax by adding back D&A, interest, stock compensation and other items, and by adding back net income attributable to noncontrolling interests, which means the measure is after the noncontrolling interest share of earnings (10-Q Q3 page:25 and page:48). The company reconciles it to operating cash flow and net income (deck Q3 page:13).

- Leverage in this handoff: total debt means long-term debt including current portion and finance lease obligations at carrying value, as in Note 4 ("2,599.1" at 30 September 2026, 10-Q Q3 page:17). The covenant definition, "consolidated total debt (less cash on hand) to Adjusted EBITDA for the trailing four quarters" with permitted pro forma adjustments (10-Q Q3 page:40), may differ in debt included, pro forma EBITDA and cash netting, and the agreement is not supplied.
- Carried forward from the readiness handoff: no credit agreement, indentures, guarantor list or ratings; covenant values not printed; deck charts not inspected.

The relevant expense block was reconciled to the printed totals. For Q3 2026 the operating expense lines (salaries and benefits 840.7, other operating expenses 245.2, occupancy 15.0, supplies 65.0, G&A 59.9, D&A 95.7) sum to the printed "Total operating expenses 1,321.5" (10-Q Q3 page:7). ### Liquidity

Liquidity at 30 September 2026 is cash and cash equivalents of $76.2 million plus about $871 million available under the $1 billion revolver, "approximately $871 million available to us under our revolving credit facility" (10-Q Q3 page:40). The availability reconciles to the commitment: 1,000 less 75.0 drawn less 53.6 letters of credit (10-Q Q3 page:20) equals 871.4. The deck shows the same split, "$871 Available $75 Drawn + $54 reserved for LCs" (deck Q3 page:11). Restricted cash of 24.0 and restricted marketable securities of 158.5 are excluded (10-Q Q3 page:40). Total liquidity on this basis is 947.2. The revolver matures 9 March 2031 (10-Q Q3 page:18), so no facility expires within twelve months of the cutoff. The only maturities within twelve months are scheduled amortization of 9.2 in the remainder of 2026 and 47.0 in 2027 on the face basis (10-Q Q3 page:17); the 12 months from 30 September 2026 therefore include 9.2 plus part of the 47.0.

Availability across the year: about $824 million at 31 Dec 2025 (10-K page:132), $726 million at 31 Mar 2026 (10-Q Q1 page:37), $746 million at 30 Jun 2026 (10-Q Q2 page:40) and $871 million at 30 Sep 2026. The rise from June to September follows the August 2026 add-on issue of 5.875% notes, whose net proceeds of about $97 million repaid revolver borrowings (10-Q Q3 page:40), and the revolver draw fell from 200.0 to 75.0 over the quarter (deck Q2 page:11 and deck Q3 page:11).

### Cash flow quality

For nine months 2026, net cash from operating activities was 957.7 against 829.6 a year earlier (10-Q Q3 page:10). Capex was 617.2 (10-Q Q3 page:10), leaving 340.5 after capex. Distributions to noncontrolling interests of 141.8, dividends of 57.9 and buybacks of 203.7 followed (10-Q Q3 page:10), so cash flow after these uses was negative 62.9. Total debt rose 108.3 over the same period (deck Q3 page:8; 10-Q Q3 page:17). For FY2025 operating cash flow of 1,175.6 less capex of 736.4, noncontrolling distributions of 152.1, dividends of 71.1 and buybacks of 158.0 left 58.0 (10-K page:165). Management's adjusted free cash flow, which deducts only maintenance capex and noncontrolling distributions, was 634.2 for nine months 2026 (deck Q3 page:14); it excludes growth capex of 441.0 on capacity expansions (deck Q3 page:8). Capex guidance for 2026 is 695 to 755 for growth (deck Q3 page:8) and 225 to 240 for maintenance, with total capex of approximately 920 to 995 (10-Q Q3 page:43). Cash taxes rose to 176.5 in nine months 2026 from 124.0 for all of 2025, partly from a 2025 underpayment (deck Q3 page:8).

Cash interest has two definitions in the sources. The 10-K reports cash paid for interest of 133.1 in FY2025 (10-K page:166) while management's "cash interest payments (net of amortization of debt discounts and fees)" are 113.6 for 2025 and 90.2 for nine months 2026 (deck Q3 page:8). The 113.6 equals the 123.2 interest expense less 9.6 of amortization (10-K page:165), so the deck measure is an accrual-based figure rather than cash paid. Interest capitalized was 17.6 in FY2025 (10-K page:196), which explains part of the gap between cash paid and expense. The Q3 10-Q omits cash paid for interest from its supplemental cash flow disclosure (10-Q Q3 page:11), so a cash-paid basis cannot be extended to Q3 2026.
### Latest quarter and after

- Financing: the 2026 Credit Agreement was signed 9 March 2026, extending maturity to 9 March 2031, with a $250.0 million draw to repay the 2022 agreement (10-Q Q3 page:18). ### Business and transaction view

Encompass Health is the largest owner and operator of inpatient rehabilitation hospitals on its own description, with 177 hospitals in 39 states and Puerto Rico at 30 September 2026, 67 of them joint ventures. There is no leveraged buyout, sponsor, acquisition or restructuring in the pack: the transactions in the period are financings, a small equity-method disposal, a litigation recovery and shareholder distributions. The business is a single segment whose revenue is set largely by government reimbursement, so the creditor risk mechanics run through Medicare rate updates, claim review and denial rules, labor cost inflation and the pace of capacity additions, rather than through sponsor behaviour. The sources show a company that has funded growth with operating cash flow and the revolver while raising dividends and buybacks, and that refinanced half of its 2028 notes into 2034 notes at a higher coupon. Credit-relevant strengths are the nondiscretionary patient base, referral dependence on acute-care hospitals that is also a joint-venture channel, and long-dated fixed-rate debt. Credit-relevant weaknesses are payor concentration, regulatory review expansion from 2027, a billing disruption that lifted bad debt reserves in Q3 2026, geographic concentration in Florida and Texas and a growth plan that consumes more cash than operations generate after distributions. Ownership, control rights and sponsor alignment cannot be assessed beyond the public-company facts, because the proxy statement is not in the pack.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

There is no sponsor transaction, acquisition or restructuring in the sources, so the transaction fact pack is a record of 2026 financing and capital events, all executed and all disclosed in the Q3 10-Q (Documentary Fact). On 9 March 2026 the company signed the 2026 Credit Agreement with Truist Bank as administrative and collateral agent, replacing the 2022 agreement that had Barclays as agent. Terms are described as substantially the same except a maturity of 9 March 2031, an undrawn fee lowered by five basis points, relaxed limits on investments, debt, liens and restricted payments, removal of a 0.10% adjustment on Term SOFR borrowings and a swingline sublimit raised from $25 million to $40 million; a $250.0 million revolver draw repaid the 2022 agreement in full (10-Q Q3 page:18). The agreement is secured by personal property of the company and its subsidiary guarantors. The agreement itself is not in the pack, so the relaxation of restricted payment and debt limits cannot be sized.

In May 2026 the company issued $500 million of 5.875% Senior Notes due 2034 at par for about $491 million of net proceeds, redeemed $400 million of the $800 million 4.50% Senior Notes due 2028 at par and repaid $100 million of revolver borrowings, recording a $3.2 million loss on early extinguishment in Q2 2026. In August 2026 it issued a further $100 million of the 2034 notes at 98.75% for about $97 million of net proceeds, used with cash to repay revolver borrowings (10-Q Q3 page:19). The liquidity effect is that revolver drawings fell to 75.0 at 30 September 2026 and availability rose to about $871 million, while total debt at carrying value rose by 108.3 over nine months 2026 (CP-1 reference; deck Q3 page:8). The coupon effect is that the weighted coupon on senior notes rises to 4.99% from 4.63% (Analyst Interpretation, see Calculations): the remaining 2028 notes at $400 million face are callable at par, and the 2034 notes are callable beginning June 2029 per the deck chart (deck Q3 page:11). The use of proceeds to retire lower-coupon debt rather than to fund distributions shows a refinancing motive, though total debt rose in the same period that dividends and buybacks rose.

Other 2026 events: a $17.9 million sale of the 50% equity interest in Gamma Knife Center at Barnes-Jewish Hospital agreed on 31 December 2025 and effective 1 January 2026, with a $17.5 million pre-tax gain in Other income (10-Q Q3 page:12); and a $21.9 million collection in February 2026 from defendants in litigation against former executive officers of the home health and hospice business spun off on 1 July 2022, producing a $16.3 million after-tax gain in discontinued operations (10-Q Q3 page:14). Both are non-recurring and are excluded or separately shown in management's adjusted measures. Subsequent events after 30 September 2026 and before the cutoff are: a dividend of $0.21 per share declared on 22 October 2026 for payment on 15 January 2027 (10-Q Q3 page:43); the Bangor, Maine and San Antonio, Texas hospitals opened in October 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:28); and raised 2026 guidance on 28 October 2026 (deck Q3 page:7). No new debt issue after 30 September 2026 appears in the sources. Ratings and pricing of the new notes against comparables cannot be assessed because no rating or quote is supplied.

### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: Medicare 66.3% and Medicare Advantage 15.7% of Q3 2026 revenue and 92% of patients admitted from acute-care hospitals (10-Q Q3 page:33; 10-K page:9). Mechanic: nondiscretionary demand supports volume, but nearly all price-setting is administrative, so a rule change reprices most revenue at once and referral channels depend on acute-care partners. Implication: revenue visibility is high on volume and low on rate; debt service capacity depends on regulatory outcomes more than on competition. Counter-evidence: the pack contains no logged conflict against this.

2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Medicare rate update of about 2.3% against assumed labor cost growth per FTE of 3.5% to 4.0% (10-Q Q3 page:31; deck Q3 page:7); bad debt reserves up to 2.7% of revenue from 1.9% (deck Q3 page:5); review expansion to 108 hospitals from 1 Jan 2027 (10-Q Q3 page:31). Mechanic: a price-cost gap and slower collections reduce EBITDA and cash conversion together. Implication: leverage of 1.88x leaves cushion, but a combined margin and collection shock would reduce the cash available for growth capex and distributions first. The conflicting account-receivable figures logged below limit how precisely cash conversion can be traced.

3. Concentration risk. Evidence: Florida and Texas beds of 3,710 out of 11,465 and a single segment (10-K page:110, page:216). Mechanic: state-level events hit a third of capacity. Implication: modest diversification within a single reimbursement system.

4. Sponsor alignment. Not applicable as a sponsor concept: the company is listed with no named sponsor. Alignment is with public shareholders through dividends and buybacks, which were partly debt-funded in nine months 2026. Implication: monitor distribution pace against free cash flow after growth capex.
5. Key uncertainties. Control and ownership detail, covenant definitions, guarantor list and the duration of the billing disruption are not evidenced.

## Calculations

- Weighted coupon on senior notes before the 2026 issues: (800 x 4.50% + 800 x 4.75% + 400 x 4.625%) = 36.00 + 38.00 + 18.50 = 92.50 on 2,000 = 4.625%, shown as 4.63%. Face amounts as in the financial base: 4.50% notes 800 before the May 2026 redemption, 4.75% notes 800, 4.625% notes 400.
- Gross annual coupon on the new 2034 notes less the retired 2028 notes: 600 x 5.875% = 35.25 less 400 x 4.50% = 18.00 gives 17.25 per year, before interest saved on the revolver.
- Florida and Texas beds: 1,718 + 1,992 = 3,710; 3,710 / 11,465 = 32.4% of licensed beds at 31 Dec 2025. Hospitals: 25 + 29 = 54 of 173 = 31.2%.
- Medicare and Medicare Advantage share, Q3 2026: 66.3% + 15.7% = 82.0%; nine months 2026: 65.7% + 16.1% = 81.8%. The 10-K reports approximately 82% for FY2025 (10-K page:23).
- Hospitals: 110 wholly owned + 67 joint ventures = 177 (10-Q Q3 page:12).

- Distributions against cash flow, nine months 2026, using the financial base: dividends 57.9 + buybacks 203.7 = 261.6; operating cash flow 957.7 less capex 617.2 less noncontrolling distributions 141.8 = 198.7; 198.7 - 261.6 = -62.9.

- Accounts receivable change: 712.0 - 619.2 = 92.8 between 31 Dec 2025 and 30 Sep 2026, against revenue growth shown in the financial base. No days-sales ratio is calculated, because period-matched revenue and a consistent receivable definition are not both supplied (see the receivable conflict).

spans.text: ## Request

Encompass Health Corp, as of 2026-11-05, credit_snapshot pathway: the fundamental credit synthesis for the consolidated registrant in USD, built only from the upstream financial base and the business and transaction fact pack, with no new source quotations. It covers business risk, financial risk and liquidity, and the gaps that limit both; relative value, security selection and recovery conclusions are out of scope.
## Sources
### Issuer sources behind the upstream handoffs
This synthesis quotes no source text. Its figures and facts come from the handoffs below, which rely on these issuer sources.
| Source file | sha256 |
| EX-99.2_2026-04-30_ehcq12026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl | 87d2e3b1959b7eb98ab23777961cb42bf7087bb7eef02c80c516da77f6348c03 |
| EX-99.2_2026-08-05_ehcq22026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl | 14fbddbdc3a3770690418d3f51a5f93d4d5adfe947473bc39ad502c3a24701ac |
| EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl | ec13580830a2a705d8e4e8dccb20f703c5d7ebb798a782d5cbe82b76c7b1cd79 |
Context (settings only, not issuer evidence): context, sha256 da12a3263f32a3446fb7ac860f9197351fa56147e40b34e0698c11063904dfbb.
### Supplied handoffs
| Module | sha256 | What this synthesis takes from it |
| CP-0 | 63fbc14da18823a4a9455191018afc3efc3c530f7a959f69feff45f5625e0fcb | Source limits: no credit agreement, indentures, guarantor list, ratings or covenant values. |
| CP-1 | d6294e2ea7978e0af0f82cdaf801b115df709e5e8f506aa1f81f648307aa83dc | Financial base: debt by instrument, liquidity, leverage, interest cover, maturities and cash flow after distributions. |
| CP-1A | 52c5e695c6c0a88340131a674e111d97ff9b3cccd8853b0ab5c524d6df383e3d | Business and transaction facts, governance reading, timeline, logged conflicts and the correction to the financial base. |
Section names in brackets below refer to the handoff sections, for example CP-1 Liquidity or CP-1A Company and operating model.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Encompass Health has a sound but reimbursement-exposed credit profile: leverage is modest and liquidity ample, while revenue depends on Medicare and Medicare Advantage and cash flow after distributions was negative in nine months 2026. | Medium | Ownership, covenant definitions, guarantors and ratings are not evidenced, and leverage figures are analyst calculations rather than covenant ratios. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Total debt was 1.88x trailing Adjusted EBITDA at Q3 2026 and net debt 1.83x. | Leverage sits well inside the 4.50x covenant maximum, though the covenant definition is not supplied. | Medium |
| Liquidity was USD 947.2 million at 30 September 2026 and the first bond maturity is the 2028 notes. | Near-term refinancing risk is low; USD 400 million face of 2028 notes remains. | High |
| Medicare and Medicare Advantage together were 82.0% of Q3 2026 revenue. | Rate updates and claim-review rules drive revenue and cash conversion more than hospital volume does. | High |

| Cash flow after capex, partner distributions, dividends and buybacks was negative USD 62.9 million in nine months 2026. | Growth and shareholder returns are partly debt-funded, so deleveraging depends on slowing either. | Medium |
| Ownership, covenant ratios, guarantor list and ratings are not supplied. | Control, covenant headroom and structural ranking cannot be confirmed. | High |
### Credit view

Encompass Health Corp is a moderately leveraged, cash-generative inpatient rehabilitation operator whose credit is sound but exposed to government reimbursement. Its strongest support is financial: total debt was 1.88x trailing Adjusted EBITDA at Q3 2026, liquidity was USD 947.2 million, and the first bond maturity is USD 400 million face of 2028 notes. Its weakest point is that Medicare and Medicare Advantage supplied 82.0% of Q3 2026 revenue, so price updates and claim-review rules can move earnings quickly, while cash flow after capex, partner distributions, dividends and buybacks was negative USD 62.9 million in nine months 2026. The outcome depends on whether review expansion from 1 January 2027 and the billing disruption erode cash conversion before the issuer slows growth capex or shareholder returns.
### Credit assessment
| Element | Content | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | Sound fundamental credit with low near-term refinancing risk and wide covenant room, offset by single-payor reimbursement risk and partly debt-funded capital returns | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 Financial base view, Liquidity, Covenants and Cash flow quality; CP-1A Company and operating model and Ownership, governance and capital allocation |

| Thesis | Encompass Health can service its USD 2,599.1 million of debt comfortably at current earnings, and the credit weakens only if reimbursement or collections deteriorate while distributions and growth capex stay high | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Same as above |

| Confidence limits | Below High because ownership is Insufficient Information, covenant definitions and agreements are not supplied, and the upstream business pack gives no explicit readiness label for this synthesis | Insufficient Information | Not applicable | CP-0 Gaps; CP-1 Gaps; CP-1A Gaps |
### Key findings

Encompass Health carries USD 2,599.1 million of total debt at carrying value at 30 September 2026, equal to 1.88x trailing four quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,379.0 million, or 1.83x net of USD 76.2 million of cash; these are analyst figures on carrying values and company-defined EBITDA, not the covenant ratios, and the covenant maximum is 4.50x [CP-1 Chart data: leverage; Covenants] (Documentary Fact for the inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the ratios).

The issuer has USD 947.2 million of liquidity: USD 76.2 million of cash plus about USD 871 million available under a USD 1,000 million revolver that matures on 9 March 2031. Its first bond maturity is USD 400 million face of 4.50% notes due 2028, followed by USD 800 million face of 4.75% notes due 2030 [CP-1 Liquidity; Debt by instrument; Chart data: debt maturities] (Documentary Fact).

Revenue is set mainly by government payors. Medicare was 66.3% and Medicare Advantage 15.7% of Q3 2026 revenue, 92% of patients are admitted from acute-care hospitals, and the 2027 Medicare rate update of about 2.3% sits against guided labor cost growth per FTE of 3.5% to 4.0% [CP-1A Company and operating model] (Documentary Fact for the mix and update, Management Language for the guidance).

The issuer funds a large capital programme and rising shareholder returns from operating cash flow and debt. For nine months 2026, operating cash flow of USD 957.7 million less capex of USD 617.2 million, partner distributions of USD 141.8 million, dividends of USD 57.9 million and buybacks of USD 203.7 million left negative USD 62.9 million, and carrying debt rose USD 108.3 million [CP-1 Cash flow quality; CP-1A Ownership, governance and capital allocation] (Documentary Fact for the components, Analyst Interpretation for the net). A correction recorded in the business pack means a Q3 2026 buyback of USD 57.9 million is supplied, which the financial base had listed as not supplied.

The 2026 refinancing pushed half of the 2028 notes out to 2034 at a higher coupon: the weighted coupon on senior notes rose to 4.99% from 4.63%, and the revolver maturity moved from October 2027 to March 2031 [CP-1A Transaction summary and new debt issues; CP-1 Debt by instrument] (Analyst Interpretation for the coupon, Documentary Fact for the dates).

Review Choice Demonstration will apply to 108 of the issuer's hospitals from 1 January 2027, and bad debt reserves reached 2.7% of Q3 2026 revenue from 1.9%, attributed by management to a billing disruption after a system conversion [CP-1A Company and operating model] (Documentary Fact; the cause is Management Language). Pre-claim review delays or denies payment, so these two items bear directly on cash conversion.

Interest cover is high: Adjusted EBITDA covered interest excluding amortization 11.7x on a trailing basis at Q3 2026 against a 3.0x covenant minimum [CP-1 Chart data: interest cover] (Analyst Interpretation); cash paid for interest in FY2025 gave 9.5x on the annual report figure, so the basis matters.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. The issuer has modest leverage, with total debt at 1.88x trailing Adjusted EBITDA at Q3 2026, and wide room under the 4.50x covenant maximum (Analyst Interpretation, CP-1 Chart data: leverage). It has ample liquidity of USD 947.2 million and no revolver expiry until March 2031 (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Liquidity). Its notes carry fixed coupons, with the first bond maturity in 2028 (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Debt by instrument). Demand is nondiscretionary, with 92% of patients admitted from acute-care hospitals, and 67 of 177 hospitals are joint ventures that tie the issuer to referring systems (Documentary Fact, CP-1A Company and operating model). Growth capex is largely discretionary, since only about USD 225 million to USD 240 million of 2026 capex is nondiscretionary against a total of about USD 920 million to USD 995 million (Documentary Fact, CP-1A Company and operating model), which gives the issuer a lever to protect cash in a downturn. Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 346.6 million in Q3 2026 against USD 300.1 million (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Financials and credit metrics).

Weaknesses. The issuer depends on one payor class for most revenue, with Medicare and Medicare Advantage at 82.0% of Q3 2026 revenue, so a single rule change reprices most of the book (Documentary Fact, CP-1A Company and operating model). Review Choice Demonstration coverage will reach 108 hospitals from 1 January 2027 and bad debt reserves are higher, which together put cash conversion at risk (Documentary Fact). Cash flow after growth capex and distributions was negative USD 62.9 million in nine months 2026, so debt rose while leverage stayed modest (Analyst Interpretation, CP-1 Cash flow quality). Adjusted EBITDA deducts net income attributable to noncontrolling interests while debt is consolidated in full, and only part of the group guarantees the notes, with the parent and guarantors producing USD 3,016.4 million of the USD 4,793.5 million nine-month 2026 revenue (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Perimeter and Findings). Florida and Texas hold 32.4% of licensed beds at 31 December 2025 (Analyst Interpretation, CP-1A Calculations). Ownership, control rights, covenant ratios, guarantor list and ratings are not evidenced (Insufficient Information, CP-0 Gaps), and missing evidence is not read as an adverse conclusion.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Reimbursement rate against labor cost | Medicare update of about 2.3% from 1 October 2026 against labor cost per FTE guided up 3.5% to 4.0% compresses margin unless volume and productivity offset | Lower EBITDA reduces covenant cushion and debt service capacity over time | Material |

| Claim review and collections | Review expansion to 108 hospitals from 1 January 2027 and bad debt reserves of 2.7% of Q3 2026 revenue delay or reduce cash receipts | Weaker cash conversion reduces cash available for debt reduction and growth | Material |

| Debt-funded capital returns and growth | Cash flow after distributions was negative USD 62.9 million for nine months 2026 while debt rose USD 108.3 million; the 2026 credit agreement relaxed restricted payment limits | Leverage tolerance depends on management restraint, since the documents permit wide distributions at current leverage | Material |

| Refinancing | USD 400 million face of 2028 notes and USD 800 million face of 2030 notes mature before the revolver in 2031; the 2028 notes are callable at par | Liquidity of USD 947.2 million covers the 2028 maturity, so refinancing risk is low unless liquidity or earnings weaken | Minor |

| Structural position | Noteholders hold guarantees from subsidiaries that guarantee the credit agreement; non-guarantors, including joint venture hospitals, produced the rest of revenue and the guarantor list is not supplied | Claims at non-guarantors could rank ahead of noteholders on those assets; size not evidenced | Minor |
| Geographic concentration | Florida and Texas hold 32.4% of licensed beds | A state-level payment or weather event has above-average effect | Minor |
| Covenant measurement | Covenant ratios are not printed and definitions differ from the analyst figures | Headroom cannot be confirmed from filings | Minor |
### Gaps propagated

Each limitation is stated once where it changes a conclusion. Upstream signals carried: the source pack lacks the credit agreement, indentures, guarantor list, ratings and covenant values, so the leverage and cover figures cannot be called covenant headroom and structural ranking is unconfirmed; ownership and control are Insufficient Information because the proxy statement is absent; and the business pack records no explicit readiness label for this synthesis, which keeps confidence at Medium. Four conflicts logged in the business pack stay unreconciled: the remaining buyback authorization, the accounts receivable balances in the annual report, the two cash interest definitions and the segment note against the income statement.
## Calculations
No new figure is introduced. Consistency checks of figures carried from the handoffs:
- Cash flow after distributions: 957.7 - 617.2 - 141.8 - 57.9 - 203.7 = -62.9.
- Weighted senior note coupon: 109.75 / 2,200 = 4.99% after and 92.50 / 2,000 = 4.63% before the 2026 issues.
- Revolver availability: 1,000 - 75.0 - 53.6 = 871.4, stated as about 871.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| Credit agreement, indentures, guarantor list and covenant values not supplied | Covenant headroom, restricted payment capacity and noteholder ranking cannot be confirmed | Leverage, cover and structural position | Material | Obtain the executed documents and a compliance certificate. |
| Ownership and control information not supplied | Control rights and related-party dealings are unknown | Governance reading | Material | Obtain the proxy statement. |
| Ratings and market quotes not supplied | No external view of default risk | Market positioning | Minor | Add ratings if a later module needs them. |

| Duration of the billing disruption and Review Choice Demonstration outcomes outside Alabama not disclosed | Cash conversion risk cannot be sized | Cash flow | Material | Track Q4 2026 and FY2026 disclosure. |
| Pro forma and covenant EBITDA definitions differ from the reported measure | Analyst leverage may differ from covenant leverage | Leverage | Minor | Compare with the compliance certificate. |
| Correction to the financial base: Q3 2026 buyback of USD 57.9 million is supplied, Q3 2025 is not | Quarterly cash flow comparison | Cash flow quality | Minor | Add the Q3 2025 quarterly report. |
## Next module

The evidence trace review should check that every figure in this synthesis matches the upstream handoffs, that the Q3 2026 buyback correction is applied consistently, that the four logged conflicts remain unreconciled, and that the ownership, covenant and guarantor gaps are carried as limitations rather than read as adverse findings.
